content.summary: Page discusses echocardiographic findings in suspected pulmonary embolism (PE) including mobile right-heart thrombi and RV dysfunction, and provides a detailed section (4.10) on compression ultrasonography (CUS) for diagnosis of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) as it relates to PE.

mobile_right_heart_thrombi.prevalence_ICU_PE: may reach 18% among PE patients in intensive care
mobile_right_heart_thrombi.clinical_significance: Essentially confirm diagnosis of PE and are associated with high early mortality, especially in patients with right ventricular (RV) dysfunction.

findings: tricuspid insufficiency jet velocity beyond values compatible with acute RV pressure overload (>3.8 m/s)
tricuspid valve peak systolic gradient >60 mmHg
echocardiography_findings_suggestive_of_.differential_consideration: Chronic thromboembolic or other pulmonary hypertension (PH) should be included in the differential diagnosis when these findings are present.

primary_points: Majority of PEs originate from lower-limb DVT; upper-limb DVT is rare.
Historic venography found DVT in ~70% of patients with proven PE.
Lower-limb CUS has largely replaced venography for diagnosing DVT.
section_4_10_compression_ultrasonography.CUS_detection_in_PE_patients: CUS shows a DVT in 30–50% of patients with PE
section_4_10_compression_ultrasonography.clinical_implication_of_proximal_DVT: Finding a proximal DVT in patients suspected of having PE is considered sufficient to warrant anticoagulant treatment without further testing.

limitations_and_technique.limited_exam: CUS can be limited to a simple four-point exam (bilateral groin and popliteal fossa) in suspected PE.
limitations_and_technique.validated_criterion: Incomplete compressibility of the vein (indicating presence of a clot) is the only validated diagnostic criterion for DVT; flow measurements are unreliable.

diagnostic_value_in_suspected_PE.positive_proximal_CUS: High positive predictive value for PE
diagnostic_value_in_suspected_PE.reported_specificity: high diagnostic specificity (96%) in one meta-analysis

section_4_10_compression_ultrasonography.combined_imaging_in_hemodynamic_instabil: In emergency patients with haemodynamic instability and suspicion of PE, combining venous ultrasound with cardiac ultrasound may increase specificity.
section_4_10_compression_ultrasonography.negative_predictive_value_example: An echocardiogram without signs of RV dysfunction plus a normal venous ultrasound excluded PE with a high (96%) negative predictive value in one study.
section_4_10_compression_ultrasonography.recommendation_reference: For further details on diagnosis and management of DVT, refer to the joint consensus document of the ESC Working Groups of Aorta and Peripheral Vascular Diseases, and Pulmonary.
